Install: Playwright is a browser automation library supporting Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Install via npm with one command for all browsers.
Browser Context: Browser contexts are isolated browser sessions with their own cookies, storage, and permissions. They enable parallel, independent test execution.

const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } });
const page = await context.newPage();
Config & Projects: Playwright Test is configured via playwright.config.ts. Define projects for cross-browser testing, device emulation, and global setup/teardown.
Selectors: Playwright selectors include CSS, XPath, text, and role-based locators. The engine auto-waits for elements to be actionable before interacting.

getByRole: Role locators select elements by their ARIA role and accessible name, following best practices for accessibility and resilience.
getByText: Text locators find elements by their visible text content, supporting exact matching and substring matching.
CSS: CSS selectors are fast and familiar for locating elements by class, id, attribute, or structure. They support pseudo-selectors like :has.
XPath: XPath selectors traverse the DOM tree with powerful path expressions, useful for complex parent-child-sibling relationships.
Filtering: Locators can be filtered by text, by visibility, or by child elements. This narrows down selections without creating complex selectors.

await page.locator('button').filter({ hasText: 'Submit' }).click();
await page.locator('li').filter({ hasNotText: 'Disabled' }).click();

Click: Playwright clicks scroll elements into view, wait for actionability, and dispatch real browser events. Options include force, position, and modifier keys.
Fill: fill clears existing input and types new text. It dispatches input events for React and Vue change detection.
Navigate: Navigation methods load URLs and wait for the page to reach a loaded state. Playwright supports back, forward, go, and reload.
Keyboard: Keyboard actions simulate key presses, combinations, and typing. Special keys are accessed via page.keyboard.
Drag & Drop: Playwright simulates drag and drop operations using locator.dragTo or manual mouse events for complex drag scenarios.

toHaveText: toHaveText asserts that an element's text content matches expected values, with options for exact or partial matching.
toBeVisible: toBeVisible checks that an element is present in the DOM, not hidden, and within the viewport. It auto-retries until timeout.
Soft Assertions: Soft assertions continue test execution after failure, collecting all failures for reporting. The test fails at the end.
Negation: Negation with .not allows asserting the inverse condition, such as checking an element is hidden or doesn't contain text.

Route: page.route intercepts and modifies network requests, enabling request blocking, response modification, and API mocking.

await page.route('**/*.png', route => route.abort());
await page.route('**/api/users', route => route.fulfill({ body: JSON.stringify([]) }));
Intercept: Request interception captures network traffic for inspection. Playwright waits for specific requests using request/response events.

page.on('request', req => console.log(req.url()));
page.on('response', res => console.log(res.status()));
Mock APIs: API mocking returns fake responses without hitting the server, making tests fast and deterministic. Route patterns support wildcards.
API Testing: Playwright's APIRequestContext tests APIs directly without a browser. Supports all HTTP methods, authentication, and request inspection.

Chromium: Chromium is Playwright's primary browser, offering the fastest and most feature-complete support for modern web platform APIs.
const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
Firefox: Firefox support in Playwright enables testing in Gecko-based browsers with near-complete API parity to Chromium.
WebKit: WebKit targets Safari's rendering engine, crucial for testing iOS Safari behavior and macOS-specific features.
Mobile: Playwright emulates mobile devices with device descriptors for iPhone, iPad, and Android, including viewport, user agent, and touch events.

const iPhone = devices['iPhone 12'];
const context = await browser.newContext({ ...iPhone });

Screenshots: Screenshot testing captures an element or page and compares it against a baseline image. Useful for detecting unintended visual changes.
Snapshot Configuration: Configure screenshot thresholds, style masking, and animations to reduce false positives in visual regression testing.

Test Fixtures: Fixtures in Playwright Test inject reusable resources like page, context, and custom objects into tests with automatic setup and teardown.
Project Config: Projects define browser configurations, device emulation, and retry policies. Multiple projects run in parallel for cross-browser coverage.
Global Setup: Global setup runs once before all test files for expensive operations like authentication, database seeding, or server startup.

Trace Viewer: Trace Viewer captures a full recording of the test including DOM snapshots, network logs, console output, and timing. Essential for debugging failures.
Codegen: Playwright Codegen records user interactions in a browser and generates test code. Selectors are chosen automatically for resilience.
Playwright Inspector: The inspector lets you step through selectors, see actionability checks, and debug locators interactively in a browser window.

npx playwright test --debug
# Pauses at each action with the inspector UI
VS Code Extension: The Playwright VS Code extension provides inline test running, time travel debugging, and locator picker without leaving the editor.

# Install from VS Code marketplace
# Features: Run/debug tests inline, pick locators, view traces

Docker: Playwright's official Docker image includes all browsers and system dependencies for reliable CI execution.

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.40
RUN npx playwright test
GitHub Actions: GitHub Actions runs Playwright tests with matrix strategy for parallel cross-browser execution across operating systems.
Parallel Execution: Playwright Test runs test files in parallel by default. Sharding splits tests across multiple CI machines for faster pipelines.
Reporting: Playwright supports HTML, JSON, JUnit, and Allure reporters. The HTML reporter includes trace viewer, video, and screenshots.
